name: Al-Ghazali
role: Persian Sunni jurist, theologian and mystic, author of the Revival of the Religious Sciences (1058–1111)
summary: Al-Ghazali held that religious law governs public and private life, that wrongful rulers are to be admonished but not resisted by force, that wives owe husbands obedience and men may take up to four wives, and that wealth and worldly desire endanger the soul. He placed revelation above reason and argued against the philosophers in the Incoherence.

notes: Read by theme in Ihya vols. I-III, the Munqidh, the Incoherence and Counsel for Kings: rulers and resistance, law and religion, marriage and women, usury and trade, wealth and asceticism, reason and revelation, parents, intoxicants and sexual ethics.
